120	"Or Yehuda" came out in the year of his Bar Mitzvah; "Divrei Yehuda" he published on the chapter "Kama Dekalim" and on

121	tractate Zavim, difficult tractates in the Shas, in memory of the completion of the Shas,

122	happy are they and happy is their portion.

123	Another grandson, among our sister's children, Adar,

124	whose hands are many also in the works of Rabbi Shmuel, published the book "Minchat Dani" on

125	tractate Berachot and the rules of the Talmud, published tractate Avot with "Darchei Avot,"

126	published "Divrei Shir" on Perek Shirah, author of "Ad Ya'aleh"

127	on the chapters of Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, all of these in addition

128	to the nephew, the dear grandson Itamar, may HaShem give him life and protect him.

129	The book "Darchei HaHalachah" was published by Rav Chadad,

130	the son-in-law, may HaShem give him life and protect him, and this too from years ago,

131	and all these are fruits of the great light of our father.

132	which I did not mention in previous lessons.

133	The great Rav, pillar of Torah, our dear brother, whose whole being is his Torah study, Rabbi David, shlita,

134	crown of the Beit Shemesh and Galilee communities, defender of Israel,

135	added this last month the book "Sefer HaZechuyot," part 2, and in addition

136	the book "Or HaHalachah," sermons on the weekly Torah portion, on

137	the book of sermons, "Sefer HaZechuyot," two separate books.

138	These, my masters, were before my eyes, and there are more in manuscript, and these I did not mention

139	in the previous lessons.

140	All these fruits are fruits of Ginosar from the

141	great light of our father, and I mention them so that I

142	and my household, my brothers, my sisters, grandsons,

143	granddaughters, will hold on to the heritage and know

144	what treasure is in our hands, and all this

145	comes from the great light, our father.

146	What I did was gather things and bring memories,

147	and what I do, and I am accustomed to say in all my Torah lessons, is that all the strength I have

148	comes from the power of "we have an old father," from the power of this father

149	who was a fire, a servant of a servant, we the sons, the grandsons,

150	the sons-in-law, and the whole family and all who hold to the path,

151	from the power of the great light.

152	All that is seen in us is the shadow of this light.

153	It is told, and our Rabbi, author of the Knesset Yechezkel, told,

154	who said in his first sermon: There was a king who decided

155	to build himself a magnificent palace, so that from all ends of the earth people would come to see

156	the beauty of the palace. Artists and builders came from every side

157	and gathered at the king's palace to receive a proposal: who will build the king's palace

158	to his satisfaction, a palace without equal, a royal chamber in a

159	uniquely special manner.

160	In the end four painters were chosen, artists in their craft.

161	The king divided the four walls of the room, the royal room, the king divided the four

162	walls, a wall for each painter.

163	He gave the four painters time, a full year, to adorn it with

164	dazzling paintings, and promised that whoever painted on the wall paintings of exceptional beauty

165	would merit a great reward.

166	All four painters rejoiced at the rare opportunity,

167	a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, to paint the king's room.

168	Already the next morning a noisy commotion was heard: three painters arrived with

169	loaded wagons, brushes, paints, and tools.

170	The three painters began to plan on sheets of paper how to adorn the walls,

171	in which colors, but the fourth painter was not there.

172	After a month of plans the painters began their work, each one striving with his best strength

173	and talent, so that there would come out from under his hand

174	a piece worthy of honor.

175	But the fourth painter was not there, the wall remained white and smooth, without color, without

176	life.

177	Half a year passed, parts of paintings were already seen, fragments of sketches, but

178	the fourth wall was not there, entirely clean.

179	The fellow painters asked the fourth painter: What is with you?

180	Do you think that without lifting a finger you will merit even a small reward?

181	And he, in his calm, smiled at them.

182	Don't worry, in the end you will see something special.

183	The year was ending, the three finished their work.

184	Each took his paints and brushes and stood before the fourth wall to see.

185	The fourth wall remained empty of any color.

186	What an affront to the king's honor.

187	They offered help to the fourth painter, but he said calmly: wait for the end.

188	The next morning the king entered, stood, stopped on the anniversary day, completely

189	amazed.

190	Eye-delighting paintings before him.

191	The three walls speak for themselves, the three walls worldly paintings

192	without equal.

193	And the fourth wall takes the breath away at its sight.

194	A wonderful blending of colors.

195	Such art no king had ever seen in his life.

196	The king stood flushed before the fourth wall.

197	The king did not stop marveling.

198	And the three painters were utterly astounded.

199	How could their fourth partner in one night paint such a wonderful work

200	in a single night?

201	While they had toiled and labored a full year.

202	They looked, all sunk in thought, studying the wonderful sight.

203	But then they understood the clever trick the fourth painter had used.

204	Instead of investing a year of work, on the last night he set up, along the length and width,

205	a mirror of glass, so that the paintings of the three walls were reflected

206	on the fourth wall.

207	They merged together and gave off colors more wonderful than all three.

208	So said our Rabbi, the Knesset Yechezkel: Our holy forefathers, the holy Geonim,

209	each and every one of them completed three walls.

210	Each one of them labored and toiled in his holy work.

211	And we, the generation of the sons, of the grandsons,

212	we, all that is in us is a mirror,

213	a reflection of what our forefathers toiled and labored and painted.

214	We have nothing of our own.

215	We ourselves are a poor, shining mirror, a mere piece of glass.

216	But all that is revealed in us is from the power of the paintings, from the power of

217	the holy work

218	of the father and the grandfather, the children and grandchildren in the family,

219	the students, who are like sons and grandsons; all the strengths we have

220	come from the power of the first painting, engraved by the greatest of

221	the painters, our righteous father, through his toil in Torah, through the attachment

222	to the Creator that he had.

223	Great attachment to the Creator, simply.

224	We all remember that at every doorway he passed, our

225	father, even in the stairwell where we lived on the third floor, without an elevator.

226	And until his last days, when he lived in the same building, he climbed the stairs,

227	and on every single floor he would kiss every single mezuzah that appeared before his eyes,

228	and pause.

229	On his way to the synagogue, when he passed in the street, he would stop beside houses and courtyards,

230	by a mezuzah, and kiss it, linger a little, and perhaps also murmur something.

231	We know that the Rambam wrote in the laws of mezuzah:

232	A person must be careful with the mezuzah, since it is an obligation upon all at all times, and every time he enters

233	and exits, he will encounter the Oneness of the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, and will remember His love,

234	and will awaken from his sleep and his foolish pursuits of the vanities of time, and will know that nothing stands forever

235	and for all eternity except knowledge of the Rock of the world, and immediately he returns to his right mind and walks

236	in the paths of the upright. This is the Rambam's language. Again: a person must be careful with the mezuzah,

237	an obligation upon all at all times; every time he enters and exits he encounters the Oneness of the Name,

238	remembers His love, awakens from his sleep and his foolish pursuits of the vanities of time, and knows

239	that nothing stands forever, for all eternity, except knowledge of the Rock of the world.
